package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package or code snippet is described in the provided report. The text discusses systemic risks from known vulnerabilities in open source software components used in medical devices and healthcare infrastructure, but does not identify or analyze any particular malicious code.

behavioral_signatures: Use of outdated or vulnerable open source components in medical device software
Lack of transparency regarding third-party software components (absence of software bill of materials)
Unpatched known vulnerabilities in healthcare infrastructure
file_indicators: Absence of a software bill of materials (SBOM)
Presence of outdated open source libraries in device firmware or application packages
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections from medical devices or hospital infrastructure
Connections to known malicious domains or IPs associated with ransomware or exploit campaigns
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor medical device and healthcare application software for the presence of outdated or vulnerable open source components. Require and review a software bill of materials (SBOM) for all deployed devices and applications. Use vulnerability scanning tools to identify known CVEs in third-party libraries. Monitor network traffic from medical devices for signs of compromise or data exfiltration.
